deprecatedRules.title: Strong profanity in the first 7 seconds
deprecatedRules.evidence: YouTube's ad guideline update log records that use of stronger profanity in the first 7 seconds of content can now be eligible to earn ad revenue. Announced 29 July 2025.
deprecatedRules.whyPeopleStillBelieveIt: In force from Nov 2022 (as a 15-second rule) and from Mar 2023 as a 7-second rule, and repeated across every creator blog and tips video since. Present in most LLM training data. This is the single most common false positive in naive policy checkers.

deprecatedRules.title: Any profanity in the first 15 seconds
deprecatedRules.evidence: Narrowed in March 2023 to strong profanity in the first 7 seconds, and then removed outright in July 2025.
deprecatedRules.whyPeopleStillBelieveIt: The original November 2022 rule, applied retroactively to already-published videos. It generated the loudest creator backlash and therefore the most surviving blog posts.
